issue_context.title: [Bug]: cgroup network interfaces should not appear in Network Interfaces
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

[Reported on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/847502280503590932/1118901743732924496/1118949811899605002).

The problem is that the network interfaces of the VMs/containers are displayed in the "Network Interfaces" section (if they were collected during the selected time period; Cloud UI).

---

The reason is: charts for all VM/container network interfaces are initially created as regular network interface charts (not associated with any VM/container). They are then deleted and new charts are re-created with cgroup-specific parameters (id, title, labels, etc.).

How it works now:

1. `proc.plugin/proc_net_dev` reads `/proc/net/dev` every second and creates charts for newly discovered interfaces (the "Network Interfaces" section).
2. `cgroups.plugin` discovers cgroups every 10 seconds and maps a virtual interface in the host namespace to an interface inside the container.
3. After mapping `cgroups.plugin` create a task for `proc.plugin/proc_net_dev`: delete existing charts for this network device and re-create them using new parameters (title, family, labels, etc).
4. `proc.plugin/proc_net_dev` does the work.


Maximum time between 1 and 4 can be up to 10 seconds (or probably even more).  

### Expected behavior

Network interfaces should never appear under Network Interfaces if they can be mapped to container interfaces.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a docker container.
2. See +1 interface in `net.net`.


### Installation method

kickstart.sh

### System info

```shell
n/a
```


### Netdata build info

```shell
netdata v1.40.0-5-g39e629e24
```


### Additional info

_No response_

review_comments:
A better solution would be to delay only specific interfaces that are likely to be container interfaces (e.g. `veth*`, `kvm*`, `cri*`), but I don't know all naming patterns. 

Considering that the problem causes [all network interface charts to be kinda broken](https://discord.com/channels/847502280503590932/1118901743732924496/1118940090396332042) when using a relatively large time range (e.g. the last N hours), I decided to just delay them all. The disadvantage of this is obvious - other virtual interfaces (e.g. bridge, bond) will have 15-second gaps after each restart. Not that bad if we assume that usually you restart ND once a day (update).
